appraisal_events.evidence: La duchesse... est incommensurable avec sa cousine. Celle-ci est exactement ce que les personnes des Halles peuvent s'imaginer qu'était la princesse de Metternich, mais la Metternich croyait avoir lancé Wagner... La princesse de Guermantes, ou plutôt sa mère, a connu le vrai. Ce qui est un prestige, sans parler de l'incroyable beauté de cette femme. Et rien que les jardins d'Esther!
appraisal_events.explanation: The unnamed interlocutor ranks the princesse de Guermantes well above her cousin the duchesse, crediting her mother's authentic connection to Wagner (unlike the merely self-flattering princesse de Metternich), her own incomparable beauty, and the exclusive, invitation-only prestige of her garden entertainments. The narrator's own parenthetical aside about society people 'crowning or dethroning' the seemingly best-established figures according to personal whim casts this ranking as capricious rather than a stable, endorsed truth.

status_effects.explanation: She is placed on an entirely different plane from her cousin the duchesse, credited with authentic cultural prestige, unmatched beauty, and access to an exclusive social world that outsiders cannot enter without her interlocutor's intervention.

ambiguities: The narrator's parenthetical remark that society people 'couronnent ou détrônent... au gré de leurs sympathies ou de leurs brouilles' frames the interlocutor's ranking of the two Guermantes women as a matter of personal caprice rather than an objective or narrator-endorsed judgment, so the elevation of the princesse is reported with ironic distance rather than straightforward endorsement.
